description: The declared corpus set. The runner asserts the directories it discovers against this list, so a corpus landed without a manifest — or a manifest landed without being declared — is a failure rather than an absence the runner reports as clean. Discovery alone cannot detect what was never added.
planned_note: Specified in CORPUS-v1-PLAN.md §2 and §3. A planned corpus that does not yet exist is expected and passes; a planned corpus that EXISTS must carry an EXPECTATIONS.json and move to `built`. `bytes-platform` and `instruments` MOVED TO BUILT at M3 batch N1E, in the same commit as their directories — ADR-0031 decision 2's N3-start freeze, asserted against `gatebraid/coverage-report@1`. `state-pipeline` MOVED TO BUILT at M3 batch O0-B1, under the operator's Batch Approval on MianliWang/gatebraid#14 (comment id 5386631542) — ADR-0031 decision 2's other freeze point, the O0-start one, asserted against `gatebraid/snapshot@1`, which that same batch landed as O0's first deliverable because the thirteen items assert tool outcomes against a snapshot-document schema that until then did not exist. Like the N1E move, this one lands in the same commit as its directory. The rule is the same in both cases and holds generally: a corpus directory and the CORPORA.json entry declaring it travel together, because the runner exits 2 on a planned corpus that exists, so any commit separating them could not evaluate the tree. The snapshot schema precedes, in its own commit, since a corpus asserting against a schema cannot land before that schema exists. The runner is green at every commit of this batch. `live-shapes` MOVED TO BUILT at M3 batch O1-B1, under the operator's REVISED Batch Approval on MianliWang/gatebraid#17 (comment id 5448556399, superseding 5445982845) — in the same commit as its directory, like both moves before it. It is a THIRD freeze point and is not one of ADR-0031 decision 2's two: those freeze §6 catalog items, and these are not §6 items at all but the four measured LIVE control-plane surfaces, frozen because the P2-S5 Gate 0 stop showed nothing in the tree recorded the shapes the state-reading toolchain actually meets. Its four schemas precede it in their own commit, for the same reason the snapshot schema preceded state-pipeline: a corpus asserting against a schema cannot land before that schema exists. THE BEHAVIOURAL HALF OF THAT BATCH'S FINDINGS IS DELIBERATELY NOT IN THE CORPUS — a short read that must be treated as incomplete, a bulk body that must end `undecidable` as a dependency answer, an absent field that must map to UNKNOWN, and the requirement that the repaired issue-states source observe CLOSED issues are assertions this runner cannot make, and they are bound instead to the repair Slice's Acceptance by that approval's clause 6. Writing them here as cases the runner would report clean is the failure mode ADR-0031's reasoning names: a corpus that looks like coverage while asserting nothing. `planned` is now empty; a future corpus is added by declaring it here before or with the commit that creates it. DETERMINACY-REPORT.md remains the single home of the item-by-item classification, its falsification case and the counts; this note deliberately does not restate them, because an enumeration copied here is a second home that drifts (ADR-0018 §3; ADR-0029 decision 3's rationale) — and in an earlier batch's first draft it did drift. ONE §6 item is frozen in NEITHER place: IN-01, re-assigned by the N1E correct-course to corpus v2 at P's start, for the reason recorded in fixtures/instruments/EXPECTATIONS.json's known_limitation.
